questions.text:
Consider the following schema:
Emp (Empcode, Name, Sex, Salary, Deptt)
A simple SQL query is executed as follows:
 SELECT Deptt FROM Emp
where sex = 'Male'
GROUP by Dept
Having avg (Salary) > {select avg (Salary) from Emp}
The output will be
questions.solution:
For each department, the query averages the salaries of male employees and keeps the department only when that average is greater than the whole organisation's average salary.

Answer: Average salary of male employees is more than the average salary of the organization

Average salary of male employee is less than the average salary of the organization
Average salary of male employee is equal to the average salary of the organization

questions.text:
Consider the following relational query on the above database:
 SELECT S.name FROM Suppliers S 
Where S.sid NOT IN (SELECT C.sid FROM Catalog C
WHERE C.pid NOT IN (SELECT P.pid FROM Parts P WHERE P.color <>'blue'))
questions.solution:
Work from the inside out:

- Innermost: pids of non-blue parts.
- Middle: catalog rows whose part is not non-blue, i.e. suppliers who supply some blue part.
- Outer: suppliers not in that list, i.e. suppliers who supply no blue part at all.

So the query returns suppliers who supply only non-blue parts (plus suppliers who supply nothing). This is closest to option 3, and none of the options is exactly right.

Answer: Options 1 and 3 (as per the ISRO key)

As per the ISRO Answer key option A and C are correct, but None of these are correct. See the detail Solution. Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Find the names of all suppliers who have supplied non-blue part.
Find the names of all suppliers who have not supplied non-blue part.
Find the names of all suppliers who have supplied only non-blue parts
Find the names of all suppliers who have not supplied only non-blue part.

questions.text: If [latex]D_1,D_2,...D_n[/latex] are domains in a relational model, then the relation is a table, which is a subset of
questions.solution:
A relation is a set of tuples [latex](d_1,\dots,d_n)[/latex] with [latex]d_i\in D_i[/latex], i.e. a subset of the Cartesian product.

Answer: [latex]D_1\times D_2\times\cdots\times D_n[/latex]

questions.text: Let R=(A,B,C,D,E,F) be a relation scheme with the following dependencies [latex]C \rightarrow F[/latex], [latex]E \rightarrow A[/latex], [latex]EC \rightarrow D[/latex], [latex]A \rightarrow B[/latex]. Which of the following is a key of R?
questions.solution:
[latex](EC)^+[/latex]: E gives A, C gives F, EC gives D, A gives B [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {A, B, C, D, E, F}.

E and C never appear on a right side, so every key must contain both. EC is the key.

Answer: EC

questions.text: The maximum length of an attribute of type text is
questions.solution:
TEXT is a variable-length type; its maximum length depends on the database system, not a fixed 127/255/256.

Answer: It is variable
